decisions.reason: As a low-cost software complement closely tied to digitalization and variable-data traceability, it is likely to stay unless its results have clearly fallen short of the firm’s now higher aspirations.

A more niche hardware coder with higher support and production demands would be harder to justify after several years if demand stayed below aspiration levels, making resource reallocation to stronger core lines plausible.
The decoding app supports the firm’s traceability direction and can be carried with modest slack as a complementary digital tool while usage and cross-selling benefits continue to be assessed.

An inline verification system fits the firm’s quality, compliance and end-to-end traceability strategy so well that a growing large firm would normally retain it unless performance was distinctly disappointing.

Print layout design software deepens the installed-system offering and is inexpensive to maintain relative to hardware, so behavioral-theory logic points to keeping it while it supports broader solution sales.
